questions.stem: Typical etomidate induction dose?
questions.explanation: Etomidate, induction: 0.2–0.3 mg/kg. 1–2 mg/kg is the ketamine IV induction dose. 0.05–0.1 mg/kg is a sedation-level amount, too low for induction. 0.5–0.7 mg/kg is above the usual etomidate range.

questions.stem: Typical subanesthetic ketamine bolus for analgesia?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, analgesic bolus: 0.1–0.5 mg/kg. 0.75–1 mg/kg is high enough to cause dissociation. 0.1–0.5 mg/kg/hr is the infusion rate, not a bolus. 1–2 mg/kg is the induction dose.

questions.stem: Typical propofol infusion rate for TIVA maintenance?
questions.explanation: Propofol, TIVA maintenance: 100–200 mcg/kg/min. 250–300 mcg/kg/min is above usual maintenance. 10–20 mcg/kg/min is too low for general anesthesia. 25–75 mcg/kg/min is the MAC sedation range.

questions.stem: Typical IV ketamine induction dose?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, IV induction: 1–2 mg/kg. 4–6 mg/kg is the IM induction dose. 2.5–3.5 mg/kg is above the usual IV range. 0.1–0.5 mg/kg is the analgesic bolus.

questions.stem: Typical propofol induction dose for a healthy adult?
questions.explanation: Propofol, adult induction: 1.5–2.5 mg/kg. 3–4 mg/kg is more than a healthy adult needs. 0.5–1 mg/kg is a reduced dose for frail patients or deep sedation. 0.2–0.3 mg/kg is the etomidate induction dose. Reduce in older or frail patients.

questions.stem: Typical propofol infusion rate for MAC sedation?
questions.explanation: Propofol, MAC sedation: 25–75 mcg/kg/min. 5–10 mcg/kg/min is too low to sedate. 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr is the dexmedetomidine infusion range. 100–200 mcg/kg/min is the TIVA maintenance range.

questions.stem: Typical subanesthetic ketamine infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, analgesic infusion: 0.1–0.5 mg/kg/hr. 0.6–1 mg/kg/hr is above the analgesic range. 1–2 mg/kg/hr is an anesthetic-level infusion. 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr is the dexmedetomidine infusion. Some PACU protocols use 0.15–0.5 mg/kg/hr.

questions.stem: Typical dexmedetomidine loading dose, given over 10 min?
questions.explanation: Dexmedetomidine, load: 1 mcg/kg. 3 mcg/kg is a high load that risks hypertension and bradycardia. 0.5 mcg/kg is half the usual load. 2 mcg/kg is double the usual load. Many clinicians skip the load.

questions.stem: Typical IM ketamine induction dose?
questions.explanation: Ketamine, IM induction: 4–6 mg/kg. 2–3 mg/kg is too low for reliable IM induction. 8–10 mg/kg is above the usual IM range. 1–2 mg/kg is the IV induction dose.

questions.stem: Typical thiopental induction dose?
questions.explanation: Thiopental, induction: 3–5 mg/kg. 1.5–2.5 mg/kg is the propofol induction dose. 6–8 mg/kg is above the usual induction range. 1–2 mg/kg is the ketamine IV induction dose.

questions.stem: Induction and sedation agent dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Correct: Ketamine, analgesic infusion 0.1–0.5 mg/kg/hr; Dexmedetomidine, load 1 mcg/kg. Incorrect: Ketamine, analgesic bolus is 0.1–0.5 mg/kg; 0.75–1 mg/kg is high enough to cause dissociation. Ketamine, IV induction is 1–2 mg/kg; 4–6 mg/kg is the IM induction dose. Dexmedetomidine, infusion is 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr; 1.5–2 mcg/kg/hr is above the usual maximum. Propofol, MAC sedation is 25–75 mcg/kg/min; 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr is the dexmedetomidine infusion range.

questions.stem: Induction and sedation agent dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Correct: Propofol, MAC sedation 25–75 mcg/kg/min; Propofol, adult induction 1.5–2.5 mg/kg; Dexmedetomidine, load 1 mcg/kg. Incorrect: Etomidate, induction is 0.2–0.3 mg/kg; 0.5–0.7 mg/kg is above the usual etomidate range. Dexmedetomidine, infusion is 0.2–0.7 mcg/kg/hr; 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/hr is too low to sedate. Ketamine, IM induction is 4–6 mg/kg; 8–10 mg/kg is above the usual IM range.

questions.stem: Induction and sedation agent dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Correct: Ketamine, IM induction 4–6 mg/kg; Thiopental, induction 3–5 mg/kg; Ketamine, IV induction 1–2 mg/kg; Propofol, TIVA maintenance 100–200 mcg/kg/min. Incorrect: Ketamine, analgesic bolus is 0.1–0.5 mg/kg; 1–2 mg/kg is the induction dose. Propofol, MAC sedation is 25–75 mcg/kg/min; 100–200 mcg/kg/min is the TIVA maintenance range.

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Propofol, TIVA maintenance 100–200 mcg/kg/min; Ketamine, IM induction 4–6 mg/kg; Ketamine, analgesic infusion 0.1–0.5 mg/kg/hr; Propofol, MAC sedation 25–75 mcg/kg/min. The extra choice, 8–10 mg/kg, is above the usual IM range (a near-miss for Ketamine, IM induction, which is 4–6 mg/kg).

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Thiopental, induction 3–5 mg/kg; Ketamine, analgesic bolus 0.1–0.5 mg/kg; Etomidate, induction 0.2–0.3 mg/kg; Propofol, adult induction 1.5–2.5 mg/kg. The extra choice, 6–8 mg/kg, is above the usual induction range (a near-miss for Thiopental, induction, which is 3–5 mg/kg).

questions.stem: Typical intranasal midazolam dose for a child?
questions.explanation: Midazolam, pediatric intranasal: 0.2–0.3 mg/kg. 0.05 mg/kg is an IV sedation-range amount. 0.6–0.8 mg/kg is above the intranasal range. 0.5 mg/kg is the oral dose.

questions.stem: Initial remimazolam dose for procedural sedation, given over 1 min?
questions.explanation: Remimazolam, initial sedation: 5 mg. 2.5 mg is the follow-up dose. 10 mg is double the initial dose. 20 mg is far above the labeled start.

questions.stem: Benzodiazepine dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Correct: Midazolam, induction 0.1–0.3 mg/kg; Remimazolam, initial sedation 5 mg; Flumazenil, increment 0.2 mg. Incorrect: Midazolam, pediatric intranasal is 0.2–0.3 mg/kg; 0.6–0.8 mg/kg is above the intranasal range. Lorazepam, status epilepticus is 0.1 mg/kg; 0.2–0.3 mg/kg is the intranasal midazolam dose. Midazolam, adult IV premed is 1–2 mg; 5–10 mg is an induction-range amount.

questions.stem: Benzodiazepine dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Correct: Midazolam, pediatric intranasal 0.2–0.3 mg/kg; Lorazepam, status epilepticus 0.1 mg/kg; Flumazenil, increment 0.2 mg; Midazolam, pediatric oral 0.5 mg/kg. Incorrect: Midazolam, adult IV premed is 1–2 mg; 3–5 mg is excessive for premedication. Remimazolam, initial sedation is 5 mg; 2.5 mg is the follow-up dose.

questions.stem: Benzodiazepine dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Correct: Midazolam, adult IV premed 1–2 mg; Flumazenil, usual cumulative 1 mg; Flumazenil, increment 0.2 mg. Incorrect: Remimazolam, initial sedation is 5 mg; 20 mg is far above the labeled start. Midazolam, pediatric oral is 0.5 mg/kg; 0.1 mg/kg is an IV-range amount, too low by mouth. Lorazepam, status epilepticus is 0.1 mg/kg; 0.02 mg/kg is too low for status epilepticus.

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Remimazolam, initial sedation 5 mg; Midazolam, pediatric oral 0.5 mg/kg; Flumazenil, usual cumulative 1 mg; Lorazepam, status epilepticus 0.1 mg/kg. The extra choice, 0.2 mg, is the single increment (a near-miss for Flumazenil, usual cumulative, which is 1 mg).

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Midazolam, induction 0.1–0.3 mg/kg; Midazolam, adult IV premed 1–2 mg; Remimazolam, initial sedation 5 mg; Midazolam, pediatric oral 0.5 mg/kg. The extra choice, 0.02–0.04 mg/kg, is the premedication range (a near-miss for Midazolam, induction, which is 0.1–0.3 mg/kg).

questions.stem: Typical cisatracurium intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Cisatracurium, intubation: 0.15–0.2 mg/kg. 0.02–0.05 mg/kg is a maintenance-range amount. 0.6 mg/kg is the rocuronium dose. 0.5 mg/kg is the atracurium dose.

questions.stem: Typical IM succinylcholine dose when there is no IV?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, IM: 4 mg/kg. 2 mg/kg is the infant IV dose. 8 mg/kg is double the IM dose. 1–1.5 mg/kg is the adult IV dose.

questions.stem: Typical rocuronium dose for rapid sequence induction?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium, RSI: 1.2 mg/kg. 0.6 mg/kg is the standard intubating dose. 0.9 mg/kg is between the standard and RSI doses. 2 mg/kg is above the usual RSI dose.

questions.stem: Typical vecuronium maintenance redose?
questions.explanation: Vecuronium, maintenance: 0.01–0.02 mg/kg. 0.1–0.2 mg/kg is the rocuronium redose. 0.1 mg/kg is the intubating dose. 0.04–0.05 mg/kg is above the usual redose.

questions.stem: Typical vecuronium intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Vecuronium, intubation: 0.1 mg/kg. 0.3 mg/kg is above the usual intubating dose. 0.6 mg/kg is the rocuronium intubating dose. 0.01–0.02 mg/kg is the maintenance redose.

questions.stem: Typical adult IV succinylcholine intubating dose?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, adult IV: 1–1.5 mg/kg. 3–4 mg/kg is the IM dose range. 0.6 mg/kg is the rocuronium intubating dose. 2 mg/kg is the infant dose.

questions.stem: Typical IV succinylcholine dose for an infant?
questions.explanation: Succinylcholine, infant IV: 2 mg/kg. 0.5 mg/kg is a laryngospasm-range amount. 4 mg/kg is the IM dose. 1 mg/kg is the dose for older children and adults.

questions.stem: Typical rocuronium maintenance redose?
questions.explanation: Rocuronium, maintenance: 0.1–0.2 mg/kg. 0.3–0.4 mg/kg is above the usual redose. 0.6 mg/kg is the intubating dose. 0.01–0.02 mg/kg is the vecuronium redose.

questions.stem: Typical cisatracurium infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Cisatracurium, infusion: 1–2 mcg/kg/min. 3–4 mcg/kg/min is above the usual range. 5–10 mcg/kg/min is an atracurium-range infusion. 0.1–0.2 mcg/kg/min is too low to maintain block.

questions.stem: Neuromuscular blocker dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Correct: Succinylcholine, laryngospasm 0.1–0.5 mg/kg; Atracurium, intubation 0.5 mg/kg; Rocuronium, maintenance 0.1–0.2 mg/kg; Vecuronium, maintenance 0.01–0.02 mg/kg. Incorrect: Succinylcholine, adult IV is 1–1.5 mg/kg; 0.6 mg/kg is the rocuronium intubating dose. Rocuronium, RSI is 1.2 mg/kg; 0.6 mg/kg is the standard intubating dose.

questions.stem: Neuromuscular blocker dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Correct: Rocuronium, intubation 0.6 mg/kg; Cisatracurium, intubation 0.15–0.2 mg/kg. Incorrect: Succinylcholine, IM is 4 mg/kg; 2 mg/kg is the infant IV dose. Succinylcholine, infant IV is 2 mg/kg; 0.5 mg/kg is a laryngospasm-range amount. Rocuronium, maintenance is 0.1–0.2 mg/kg; 0.6 mg/kg is the intubating dose. Vecuronium, maintenance is 0.01–0.02 mg/kg; 0.04–0.05 mg/kg is above the usual redose.

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Vecuronium, intubation 0.1 mg/kg; Cisatracurium, infusion 1–2 mcg/kg/min; Atracurium, intubation 0.5 mg/kg; Vecuronium, maintenance 0.01–0.02 mg/kg. The extra choice, 0.15–0.2 mg/kg, is the cisatracurium dose (a near-miss for Atracurium, intubation, which is 0.5 mg/kg).

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Rocuronium, intubation 0.6 mg/kg; Atracurium, intubation 0.5 mg/kg; Cisatracurium, infusion 1–2 mcg/kg/min; Succinylcholine, laryngospasm upper limit 1 mg/kg. The extra choice, 0.1–0.2 mcg/kg/min, is too low to maintain block (a near-miss for Cisatracurium, infusion, which is 1–2 mcg/kg/min).

questions.stem: Low-dose naloxone infusion rate for neuraxial opioid pruritus?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, pruritus infusion: 0.25–1 mcg/kg/hr. 2.5–5 mg is the nalbuphine pruritus dose. 3–5 mcg/kg/hr is enough to reverse analgesia. 1–2 mcg/kg is a bolus for respiratory depression.

questions.stem: Typical neostigmine reversal dose?
questions.explanation: Neostigmine, reversal: 0.04–0.07 mg/kg. 0.01–0.02 mg/kg is closer to the glycopyrrolate pairing dose. 0.5–1 mg/kg is the edrophonium dose. 0.1–0.15 mg/kg is above the ceiling dose.

questions.stem: Usual maximum neostigmine dose for reversal?
questions.explanation: Neostigmine, maximum: 5 mg. 7 mg is above the maximum. 10 mg is double the maximum. 2.5 mg is half the usual maximum.

questions.stem: Sugammadex dose for immediate reversal after an RSI dose of rocuronium?
questions.explanation: Sugammadex, immediate reversal: 16 mg/kg. 8 mg/kg is half the immediate dose. 4 mg/kg is the deep block dose. 32 mg/kg is double the immediate dose.

questions.stem: Typical pediatric IV atropine dose?
questions.explanation: Atropine, pediatric: 0.02 mg/kg. 0.05 mg/kg is above the usual dose. 0.1 mg/kg is the pediatric adenosine dose. 0.01 mg/kg is the pediatric epinephrine arrest dose.

questions.stem: Typical adult glycopyrrolate antisialagogue dose?
questions.explanation: Glycopyrrolate, antisialagogue: 0.1–0.2 mg. 1 mg is the atropine bradycardia dose. 0.4–0.6 mg is a reversal-pairing amount. 0.02–0.04 mg is too little to dry secretions.

questions.stem: Sugammadex dose for moderate block (TOF count 2)?
questions.explanation: Sugammadex, moderate block: 2 mg/kg. 1 mg/kg is half the moderate block dose. 16 mg/kg is the immediate reversal dose. 4 mg/kg is the deep block dose.

questions.stem: Typical initial IV naloxone dose for opioid overdose?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, IV overdose: 0.4 mg. 40 mcg is the postop titration dose. 0.1 mg is a small titration step. 4 mg is the intranasal dose.

questions.stem: Atropine dose paired with edrophonium?
questions.explanation: Atropine with edrophonium: 7–10 mcg/kg. 2–3 mcg/kg is too low to offset edrophonium. 30–40 mcg/kg is enough to cause marked tachycardia. 20 mcg/kg is the pediatric bradycardia dose.

questions.stem: Typical naloxone titration dose for postoperative respiratory depression?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, postop titration: 40 mcg. 10 mcg is too small to restore breathing. 4 mg is the intranasal dose. 0.4 mg is the overdose starting dose.

questions.stem: Adult ACLS atropine dose for symptomatic bradycardia?
questions.explanation: Atropine, adult bradycardia: 1 mg. 3 mg is the cumulative maximum. 0.1 mg is a small amount that can cause paradoxical slowing. 0.5 mg is the older ACLS starting dose.

questions.stem: Typical adult physostigmine dose for central anticholinergic syndrome?
questions.explanation: Physostigmine, adult: 0.5–2 mg. 0.1–0.2 mg is too low to reverse the syndrome. 4–5 mg is above the usual dose. 0.2 mg is the flumazenil increment.

questions.stem: Standard intranasal naloxone dose?
questions.explanation: Naloxone, intranasal: 4 mg. 40 mcg is the postop IV titration dose. 0.2 mg is the flumazenil increment. 0.4 mg is the IV overdose start.

questions.stem: Sugammadex dose for deep block (PTC 1–2 or more, TOF 0)?
questions.explanation: Sugammadex, deep block: 4 mg/kg. 2 mg/kg is the moderate block dose. 16 mg/kg is the immediate reversal dose. 8 mg/kg is between the deep and immediate doses.

questions.stem: Reversal agent dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 5)
questions.explanation: Correct: Glycopyrrolate, antisialagogue 0.1–0.2 mg; Neostigmine, maximum 5 mg; Naloxone, postop titration 40 mcg; Naloxone, intranasal 4 mg; Naloxone, pruritus infusion 0.25–1 mcg/kg/hr. Incorrect: Naloxone, IV overdose is 0.4 mg; 40 mcg is the postop titration dose.

questions.stem: Reversal agent dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 5)
questions.explanation: Correct: Naloxone, postop titration 40 mcg; Naloxone, IV overdose 0.4 mg; Atropine, adult bradycardia 1 mg; Naloxone, intranasal 4 mg; Atropine, pediatric 0.02 mg/kg. Incorrect: Sugammadex, deep block is 4 mg/kg; 16 mg/kg is the immediate reversal dose.

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Atropine with edrophonium 7–10 mcg/kg; Glycopyrrolate, antisialagogue 0.1–0.2 mg; Neostigmine, maximum 5 mg; Physostigmine, adult 0.5–2 mg. The extra choice, 0.02–0.04 mg, is too little to dry secretions (a near-miss for Glycopyrrolate, antisialagogue, which is 0.1–0.2 mg).

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Glycopyrrolate per 1 mg neostigmine 0.2 mg; Atropine, adult bradycardia 1 mg; Glycopyrrolate, antisialagogue 0.1–0.2 mg; Neostigmine, maximum 5 mg. The extra choice, 0.5 mg, is the older ACLS starting dose (a near-miss for Atropine, adult bradycardia, which is 1 mg).

questions.stem: Typical remifentanil maintenance infusion with a volatile or propofol?
questions.explanation: Remifentanil, infusion: 0.05–0.25 mcg/kg/min. 0.5–1 mcg/kg/min is above typical maintenance. 0.01–0.02 mcg/kg/min is too low to matter. 0.5–2 mcg/kg/hr is the fentanyl infusion.

questions.stem: Typical IV hydromorphone increment for an opioid-naive adult?
questions.explanation: Hydromorphone, PACU increment: 0.2–0.5 mg. 0.05–0.1 mg is too small to help. 1–2 mg is a large dose for an opioid-naive patient. 2–4 mg is the morphine increment.

questions.stem: Typical fentanyl infusion rate?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, infusion: 0.5–2 mcg/kg/hr. 5–10 mcg/kg/hr is excessive. 0.1–0.2 mcg/kg/hr is too low. 0.05–0.25 mcg/kg/min is the remifentanil infusion.

questions.stem: IV meperidine dose range for postoperative shivering?
questions.explanation: Meperidine, shivering: 12.5–50 mg. 2.5–5 mg is the nalbuphine pruritus dose. 150 mg is above any shivering dose. 75–100 mg is an analgesic-range dose. The usual single dose is 25 mg.

questions.stem: Typical IV fentanyl increment in PACU for an opioid-naive adult?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, PACU increment: 25–50 mcg. 0.2–0.5 mg is the hydromorphone increment. 5–10 mcg is too small to help. 100–150 mcg is a large bolus for an opioid-naive patient.

questions.stem: Usual single IV meperidine dose for postoperative shivering?
questions.explanation: Meperidine, usual shivering dose: 25 mg. 100 mg is excessive for shivering. 5 mg is too small to stop shivering. 75 mg is an analgesic dose. The range is 12.5–50 mg.

questions.stem: Typical alfentanil bolus for a brief procedure?
questions.explanation: Alfentanil, bolus: 10–20 mcg/kg. 1–3 mcg/kg is the fentanyl dose. 0.1–0.5 mcg/kg is the sufentanil dose. 50–75 mcg/kg is induction-level alfentanil.

questions.stem: Typical IV nalbuphine dose for neuraxial opioid pruritus?
questions.explanation: Nalbuphine, pruritus: 2.5–5 mg. 10–20 mg is an analgesic dose with more mu reversal. 0.5 mg is too small. 40 mcg is the naloxone titration dose.

questions.stem: Typical intrathecal morphine dose for cesarean delivery?
questions.explanation: Morphine, intrathecal cesarean: 100–150 mcg. 10–25 mcg is the intrathecal fentanyl dose. 2–3 mg is the epidural dose. 300–500 mcg is above the usual range. Some centers use 50–100 mcg.

questions.stem: Typical intrathecal fentanyl dose?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, intrathecal: 10–25 mcg. 100–150 mcg is the intrathecal morphine dose. 2–5 mcg is too small. 50–100 mcg is an epidural bolus-range dose.

questions.stem: Typical IV morphine increment for an opioid-naive adult?
questions.explanation: Morphine, PACU increment: 2–4 mg. 0.2–0.5 mg is the hydromorphone increment. 0.5–1 mg is too small for most adults. 8–10 mg is a large bolus.

questions.stem: Typical fentanyl dose to blunt laryngoscopy?
questions.explanation: Fentanyl, induction: 1–3 mcg/kg. 0.1–0.5 mcg/kg is the sufentanil range. 5–10 mcg/kg is high-dose cardiac-range dosing. 10–20 mcg/kg is the alfentanil bolus.

questions.stem: Opioid dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: Correct: Remifentanil, bolus 0.5–1 mcg/kg; Hydromorphone, PACU increment 0.2–0.5 mg; Alfentanil, bolus 10–20 mcg/kg. Incorrect: Nalbuphine, pruritus is 2.5–5 mg; 10–20 mg is an analgesic dose with more mu reversal. Methadone, induction is 0.1–0.2 mg/kg; 0.5–1 mg/kg is excessive. Fentanyl, intrathecal is 10–25 mcg; 2–5 mcg is too small.

questions.stem: Opioid dosing: which doses are correct? (Select 4)
questions.explanation: Correct: Morphine, epidural 2–3 mg; Fentanyl, PACU increment 25–50 mcg; Morphine, intrathecal cesarean 100–150 mcg; Fentanyl, intrathecal 10–25 mcg. Incorrect: Meperidine, usual shivering dose is 25 mg; 5 mg is too small to stop shivering. Hydromorphone, PACU increment is 0.2–0.5 mg; 1–2 mg is a large dose for an opioid-naive patient.

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Fentanyl, induction 1–3 mcg/kg; Sufentanil, induction 0.1–0.5 mcg/kg; Morphine, PACU increment 2–4 mg; Alfentanil, bolus 10–20 mcg/kg. The extra choice, 0.2–0.5 mg, is the hydromorphone increment (a near-miss for Morphine, PACU increment, which is 2–4 mg).

questions.stem: Match each drug and use to its typical dose.
questions.explanation: Typical doses: Fentanyl, induction 1–3 mcg/kg; Morphine, PACU increment 2–4 mg; Methadone, induction 0.1–0.2 mg/kg; Nalbuphine, pruritus 2.5–5 mg. The extra choice, 0.1–0.5 mcg/kg, is the sufentanil range (a near-miss for Fentanyl, induction, which is 1–3 mcg/kg).

questions.stem: IV amisulpride dose for PONV prophylaxis?
questions.explanation: Amisulpride, prophylaxis: 5 mg. 2.5 mg is half the prophylaxis dose. 10 mg is the rescue dose. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose.

questions.stem: Typical haloperidol dose for PONV?
questions.explanation: Haloperidol, PONV: 0.5–2 mg. 2.5–5 mg is above the low-dose antiemetic range. 4–8 mg is the dexamethasone dose. 5–10 mg is an agitation dose.

questions.stem: Typical IV famotidine dose for aspiration prophylaxis?
questions.explanation: Famotidine, IV: 20 mg. 50 mg is the old IV ranitidine dose. 10 mg is the metoclopramide dose. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose.

questions.stem: Adult dexamethasone PONV dose?
questions.explanation: Dexamethasone, adult PONV: 4–8 mg. 1–2 mg is too low. 10–20 mg is steroid dosing for airway edema. 0.5–2 mg is the haloperidol PONV dose.

questions.stem: Adult ondansetron PONV dose?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron, adult: 4 mg. 10 mg is the metoclopramide dose. 8 mg is double the PONV dose. 0.625 mg is the low droperidol dose.

questions.stem: Typical IV promethazine dose for PONV?
questions.explanation: Promethazine, PONV: 6.25–12.5 mg. 0.5–2 mg is the haloperidol dose. 25–50 mg is an older dose with more sedation and tissue risk. 1–2 mg is too low.

questions.stem: Typical IV metoclopramide dose before induction?
questions.explanation: Metoclopramide, IV: 10 mg. 25–50 mg is the diphenhydramine dose. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose. 20 mg is the famotidine dose.

questions.stem: Typical droperidol dose for PONV?
questions.explanation: Droperidol, PONV: 0.625–1.25 mg. 2.5–5 mg is older higher doses with more sedation. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose. 0.1–0.2 mg is too low.

questions.stem: Pediatric ondansetron dose (max 4 mg)?
questions.explanation: Ondansetron, pediatric: 0.1 mg/kg. 0.15 mg/kg is the pediatric dexamethasone dose. 0.05 mg/kg is half the usual dose. 0.2 mg/kg is double the usual dose.

questions.stem: Typical adult IV diphenhydramine dose?
questions.explanation: Diphenhydramine, IV: 25–50 mg. 5–10 mg is too low. 6.25–12.5 mg is the promethazine dose. 100 mg is excessive.

questions.stem: Pediatric dexamethasone PONV dose?
questions.explanation: Dexamethasone, pediatric: 0.15 mg/kg. 0.5 mg/kg is a croup-range dose. 0.05 mg/kg is too low. 0.1 mg/kg is the pediatric ondansetron dose.

questions.stem: Oral aprepitant dose for PONV prophylaxis?
questions.explanation: Aprepitant, PONV: 40 mg. 4 mg is the ondansetron dose. 80 mg is the chemotherapy day 2–3 dose. 125 mg is the chemotherapy day-1 dose.

questions.stem: Scopolamine transdermal patch strength?
questions.explanation: Scopolamine, patch: 1.5 mg. 0.4 mg is an older IV scopolamine dose. 1 mg is the amount delivered over 72 hr, not the patch content. 3 mg is two patches.

questions.stem: Typical oral sodium citrate volume before cesarean?
